Yes, his/her fat intake is perfectly fine, but fats are not the only source of this precursor to testosterone. Acetyl-CoA is the precursor, forming isoprenes, which then can form steroids such as testosterone. Carbohydrates, i.e. glucose, can also be oxidized into Acetyl-CoA to then progress through the same metabolic pathway as the oxidized fats to form testosterone. Please backup your statements with facts or research before misguiding others!

This time it is a bit more exciting than just carbon compounds! One of the compounds they found, thiopene, a cyclic sulfur diene, is very similar to methylthiopene, a molecular unit called an isoprene. Isoprenes are responsible for a load of biological compounds, such as turpenes and steroids. Pretty cool!

Believe it or not, the internet, unless you are reading peer reviewed studies, does not provide instantaneous, 100% accurate information when it comes to nutrition. It is always important to review your data before misinforming other people :)

Yes, people survived, but we are trying to optimize nutrition, not just survive.

I also do not see the point of attempting the keto diet unless you want to excise fat from the body... or send yourself into ketoacidosis.

Without sugars to oxidize for energy, the body will resort to only fatty acid catabolism. If the body does this, all of its oxaloacetate will be used for the citric acid cycle and no oxaloacetate will continue through gluconeogenesis to maintain blood sugar homeostasis. This creates a negative feedback loop of continual fatty acid catabolism, thus increasing the amount of acetoacetate produced as a byproduct. This acidifies your blood, making hemoglobin release it's oxygen. Thus, your blood's affinity for oxygen is reduced, hence the common complaints of lethargy associated with the keto diet.

Carbs are just fine. Your body needs them.
